# Temple Scroll Column 19 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 19 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 19:2 — "dash it upon the altar round about" vs. "dash it against the altar on all sides" vs. "splash it against all sides"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "dash it upon the altar round about" | Literal zaraqta al ha-mizbeach saviv |
| LOGOS | "dash it against the altar on all sides" | "Against" and "on all sides" clarify the action |
| PNEUMA | "splash it against all sides of the altar" | "Splash" conveys the vigorous throwing action |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Dash against the altar on all sides" accurately conveys the zaraq action (throwing/tossing blood, not merely sprinkling). PNEUMA's "splash" is too informal for ritual legislation. EMET's "round about" is archaic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:5 — "make smoke" vs. "turn into smoke" vs. "burn" — hiqtir (recurring)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "make the whole ram smoke upon the altar" | Literal hiqtir; preserves causative |
| LOGOS | "turn the entire ram into smoke on the altar" | Standard Milgrom rendering |
| PNEUMA | "Burn the entire ram on the altar" | Simple "burn" for accessibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "turn into smoke" (LOGOS), consistent with Column 18 ruling. The distinction between hiqtir and saraf must be maintained.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Consistent with Col. 18 precedent.

---

## 19:9 — "great toe" vs. "big toe" — bohen regel

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the great toe of their right foot" | "Great toe" — archaic but traditional |
| LOGOS | "the big toe of their right foot" | Modern standard English |
| PNEUMA | "the big toe of their right foot" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "big toe" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). "Big toe" is standard modern English. "Great toe" (EMET) is archaic and potentially confusing.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 19:12 — "he shall be holy" vs. "he shall be consecrated" vs. "this will consecrate him"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he shall be holy, he and his garments" | Literal ve-qadash hu u-vegadav |
| LOGOS | "he shall be consecrated — he and his vestments" | "Consecrated" for ritual qadash |
| PNEUMA | "this will consecrate him and his garments" | Active voice; causal connection explicit |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Consecrated" correctly renders the resultative sense of qadash in this ritual context — the sprinkling achieves consecration. EMET's "be holy" is too abstract for the immediate ritual result. PNEUMA's restructuring loses the declarative force.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:13 — "fat tail" vs. "broad fat tail" — alyah

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the fat tail" | Standard rendering of alyah |
| LOGOS | "the fat tail" | Same as EMET |
| PNEUMA | "the broad fat tail" | Adds "broad" to describe the distinctive Near Eastern sheep tail |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "fat tail" (EMET/LOGOS). The alyah is already well understood in biblical scholarship as the broad fat tail of the fat-tailed sheep breed. Adding "broad" (PNEUMA) is unnecessary and not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
